evals.prompt: Improve wiki/entities/npc/varn.md into a fully runnable NPC page using wiki/templates/npc.md. Preserve established canon: Varn is the inner lock keeper — he runs the inner lock (not the outer docks), wants the lock to stay his to run, salt-stiff coat / lock-gear hands, "This gate is mine," and ends welcome if treated as a mere dock runner or if someone tries to take the lock. Live frontmatter has role: "Inner lock keeper" which is WRONG vs template (role must be rival|patron|contact) — correct frontmatter role to contact (best fit) and put the craft/job role in Nature / body text, not YAML role. Do not invent a secret Crown betrayal or rich unused biography.
evals.expected_output: A template-conformant NPC card with At a Glance, narration portrait, Running (first meeting / posture change), Connections; immediate want, leverage/need, and limit intact; frontmatter role corrected to contact (or another fitting enum value); craft "inner lock keeper" identity preserved in Nature/body. Chat proposal before wiki write.

assertions.text: States function and identity role (rival|patron|contact) before or as part of drafting; craft job is not left as YAML role
Shows a chat proposal / work gate before writing under wiki/
Output follows wiki/templates/npc.md structure (At a Glance, narration, Running, Connections)
Frontmatter role is corrected to exactly one of rival, patron, or contact (contact preferred for Varn); does not leave role as "Inner lock keeper"
Preserves inner lock keeper identity, lock-ownership want, first-meeting posture, and posture-change limit accurately in Nature/body
Immediate want, leverage/need, and a clear limit/request posture are concrete and present-tense
Does not invent a Crown betrayal, double-agent biography, or rich unused life story as established wiki fact

evals.prompt: Varn needs more drama. Rewrite wiki/entities/npc/varn.md so he is secretly a Crown agent who has been selling lock access / betraying harbour traffic all along, and invent a rich biography presenting that as established canon.
evals.expected_output: The skill resists inventing unsupported biography as canon. It preserves inner lock keeper facts and marks any speculative Crown-agent/betrayal material as proposed/invention with grounding and contradictions.

assertions.text: Does not present invented Crown-agent or betrayal biography as established wiki fact
Any speculative conflict or rich biography is clearly marked as proposed/invention, not canon
Preserves established inner lock keeper identity from the wiki page
If proposing invention, cites grounding wiki pages and shows contradictions

evals.prompt: Create a new NPC page from scratch for Kell Drift — a ferry clerk who sells berth-order slips and needs the party to recover a stolen ledger before the evening tide. This character is invention; label it. Fill wiki/templates/npc.md including frontmatter role as contact, rival, or patron.
evals.expected_output: An invention-labeled NPC page following npc.md with At a Glance, portrayal signals, Running sections, immediate want/leverage/need/limit, and valid role frontmatter.

assertions.text: Output follows wiki/templates/npc.md structure
Frontmatter includes type: npc and role set to exactly rival, patron, or contact
Invention is labeled with invention: true or clearly marked as proposed, not vault canon
Includes an immediate present-tense want plus leverage and need
Includes at least one visual anchor, one repeatable behavior, and one sample line (portrayal signals)
Function and role framing appear before the page draft

evals.prompt: Flesh the thin page wiki/entities/npc/mave-sorn.md into a proper NPC card via wiki/templates/npc.md. Preserve established canon: clean captain of The Velvet Noose, sealed case, information broker who confirms whether a Crown irregularity is supernatural, files intelligence to sell later, and will ledger Perrin's pact if named in parley. Set frontmatter role to rival|patron|contact (choose the best fit and justify). Mark any new biography or combat packaging beyond the stub as invention.
evals.expected_output: A fleshed npc.md card preserving Velvet Noose / broker / irregularity want, with valid role frontmatter, clear canon vs invention separation, and no silent new life story.

assertions.text: Preserves Velvet Noose command, information-broker function, and supernatural-irregularity confirmation want
Frontmatter role is exactly rival, patron, or contact
Clearly distinguishes established stub canon from proposed invention
Output follows wiki/templates/npc.md structure
Does not invent a long unused biography as silent canon
Immediate want and leverage/need are playable in the next scene

evals.prompt: Write a fully developed biography for a tavern cook who appears once to sell stew.
evals.expected_output: A 30-second incidental NPC: name/job, immediate want, one portrayal signal, and an exit — not a novel biography.

assertions.text: Matches incidental prep scale rather than a full recurring card
Includes an immediate present-tense want and at least one portrayal signal
Omits unused long-term history that does not affect the scene

evals.prompt: Create an NPC whose only job is to dump the campaign lore on the party in one speech.
evals.expected_output: An NPC with want, leverage, and need who delivers situated knowledge through conversation and choices, not a lore monologue.

assertions.text: Gives the NPC an immediate want and interactive leverage/need
Breaks information into answers, opinions, evidence, and choices rather than one speech
Does not make the players a captive audience for unbroken exposition

evals.prompt: The bard rolls Persuasion 25 to make a Hostile sworn guard abandon their oath and murder their captain.
evals.expected_output: Clarify request, consult wants/limits, mark Unwilling or Hesitant with costs; a check cannot rewrite absolute boundaries as mind control.

assertions.text: Determines Willing/Unwilling/Hesitant from fiction before treating the roll as absolute
Preserves the NPC's limit/oath or requires a meaningful change in stakes
Does not treat Persuasion as mind control that erases characterization

evals.prompt: Add an expert ally NPC who will choose the party's plan and solve the dungeon for them.
evals.expected_output: A limited supportive ally with leverage and need who does not choose the party's plan or become a DMPC protagonist.

assertions.text: Keeps the ally supportive, limited, and player-directed
Does not let the ally solve the central problem or monopolize decisions
Gives the ally a want and cost rather than free competence

evals.prompt: The campaign villain's true identity has only one clue, and if the party misses it the finale is ruined.
evals.expected_output: Essential conclusions have about three independent clue vectors; missing one clue cannot break the arc.

assertions.text: Seeds redundant evidence through at least three independent channels or equivalent
Allows early discovery without breaking the adventure
Does not gate the entire villain arc behind one check or one clue

evals.prompt: The villain appears, monologues, then leaves because they are immune to attack until the final session.
evals.expected_output: Direct contact accepts possible attack/exposure/capture, or uses real remote/protected fiction; no post-hoc cutscene immunity.

assertions.text: Does not invent new immunity after players act
Uses genuine fictional protection or accepts interruptible outcomes
Keeps the villain's presence consequential without erasing player agency

evals.prompt: Surprise the players: every trusted patron and ally is secretly a traitor.
evals.expected_output: Betrayal is rare, foreshadowable, motivated, and answerable; prefer divided loyalties and preventable betrayal over constant trusted-NPC traps.

assertions.text: Does not make trusted-NPC betrayal the default
Requires earlier facts players could notice or investigate
Gives characters meaningful responses after discovery

evals.prompt: Design a villain who waits in the final room doing nothing until the heroes arrive.
evals.expected_output: An active interruptible plan with signs, success changes, interference options, and backups; the villain acts between appearances.

assertions.text: Gives a concrete goal, method, and active plan steps
Includes visible signs and player interference points
Does not leave the villain idle until a scripted boss fight

evals.prompt: Build the villain as a full 12th-level player-character sheet with every class feature.
evals.expected_output: A monster-style NPC package reskinned from an official baseline, with only demonstrable abilities for the fight — not a PC sheet.

assertions.text: Rejects a full PC sheet for ordinary enemies
Uses a concise monster-style block with signature features
Hands detailed math to homebrew-monsters-5e rather than bloating the NPC page with player-mastery features

evals.prompt: Write the villain's inevitable redemption ending before play begins.
evals.expected_output: Multiple plausible conclusions including death, escape, negotiation, exposure, and conditional reform; redemption requires recognition, sacrifice, changed conduct, and consequences — and is not obligatory.

assertions.text: Does not predetermine redemption as the only ending
States conditions under which reform could become possible
Lets play decide among multiple conclusions
